overview.headline: Continuous movement of water between Earth and atmosphere

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the water cycle involves continuous circulation between Earth and atmosphere.
keyPoints.quote: The hydrologic cycle involves the continuous circulation of water in the Earth-Atmosphere system.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that evaporation is the change of liquid water into gas.
keyPoints.quote: Evaporation is the change of state in a substance from a liquid to a gas.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that transpiration moves water from plants through stomata into air.
keyPoints.quote: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from plants through stomata.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that release of heat during condensation aids formation of hurricanes.
keyPoints.quote: This release of heat aids in the formation of hurricanes.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that precipitation can fall as rain, hail, snow or sleet.
keyPoints.quote: Precipitation can be in the form of rain, hail, snow, or sleet.

keyTerms.gloss: Change of liquid water to gas requiring energy
keyTerms.quote: Evaporation is the change of state in a substance from a liquid to a gas.

keyTerms.gloss: Evaporation of water from plants through leaf openings
keyTerms.quote: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from plants through stomata.

keyTerms.gloss: Process where water vapor changes into liquid clouds or dew
keyTerms.quote: Condensation is the process whereby water vapor is changed into a liquid state.

keyTerms.gloss: Water falling as rain, hail, snow or sleet
keyTerms.quote: Precipitation can be in the form of rain, hail, snow, or sleet.

keyTerms.gloss: Excess water flowing over saturated ground toward rivers and lakes
keyTerms.quote: Runoff occurs when there is excessive precipitation and the ground is saturated (cannot absorb any more water).

keyTerms.gloss: Temperature where air becomes saturated and dew can form
keyTerms.quote: Foggy conditions often occur when air temperature and dew point are equal.
